literal: He died; his posthumous title was Kang.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Kang.

literal: His son Luan inherited.
idiomatic: His son Luan inherited.

literal: Luan, courtesy name Xuanming, was eight chi in height; his belt measured ten arm-spans around.
idiomatic: Luan, courtesy name Xuanming, stood eight chi; his belt measured ten arm-spans around.

literal: He was famed for martial arts and repeatedly served as Grand General of the Northern Capital.
idiomatic: He was famed for martial arts and repeatedly served as grand general of the northern capital.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was made Bearer of the Staff and Southern Campaign Grand General.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was made bearer of the staff and southern campaign grand general.

literal: With Grand General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yangwu and Li Zuo he attacked Zhiyang but could not take it; defeated, they withdrew; he was reduced to Prince of Dingxiang County.
idiomatic: With Grand General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yangwu and Li Zuo he attacked Zhiyang but could not take it; defeated, they withdrew; he was reduced to Prince of Dingxiang County.

literal: Later, for merit in holding the rear, he was restored to his original enfeoffment.
idiomatic: Later, for merit in holding the rear, he was restored to his original enfeoffment.

literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was governor of Ding.

literal: Luan loved and delighted in Buddha's Way; he repaired Buddhist temples, urged and led the common people, and greatly labored them with earth and timber; public and private were troubled and he was much a nuisance to men.
idiomatic: Luan loved Buddha's Way; he repaired temples, urged and led the people, and greatly labored them with earth and timber; public and private were troubled and he was much a nuisance.

literal: When Emperor Xuanwu heard of it, an edict stripped his salary for one cycle.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu heard of it, an edict stripped his salary for one cycle.

literal: He died; his posthumous title was Huai.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Huai.

literal: His son Hui, courtesy name Xianshun, had slight knowledge of literature and history and considerable talent for administration.
idiomatic: His son Hui, courtesy name Xianshun, had slight knowledge of literature and history and considerable talent for administration.

literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he inherited the enfeoffment and was Administrator of Henei.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he inherited the enfeoffment and was administrator of Henei.

literal: In the commandery he was clear and orderly and had a reputation in the age.
idiomatic: In the commandery he was clear and orderly and had a reputation in the age.

literal: Under Emperor Ming he was Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was governor of Bing.

literal: Earlier, within the province's borders summer frost had fallen; those secure in their livelihoods were few; Hui at once opened the granaries to relieve them; civil and military officials all together remonstrated and stopped him.
idiomatic: Earlier, within the province summer frost had fallen; those secure in livelihood were few; Hui at once opened the granaries to relieve them; civil and military officials all remonstrated and stopped him.

literal: Hui said: "Formerly Ji Changru, though only a commandery administrator, still opened the granary to save men from disaster and hardship.
idiomatic: Hui said, "Formerly Ji Changru, though only a commandery administrator, still opened the granary to save men from disaster.

literal: How much more I, a close kin of the imperial house, entrusted with a great frontier—how can I cling to the law and not save men in distress?"
idiomatic: How much more I, close kin of the house, entrusted with a great frontier—how can I cling to the law and not save men in distress?"

literal: He gave out first and memorialized afterward.
idiomatic: He gave out first and memorialized afterward.

literal: Emperor Ming praised him and added the title General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: Emperor Ming praised him and added the title General Who Pacifies the North.

literal: The mountain Hu of Fen Province had long plundered heavily; from the time Hui was in the province the Hu groups warned one another not to disturb neighboring provinces.
idiomatic: The mountain Hu of Fen had long plundered heavily; from the time Hui governed the province the Hu groups warned one another not to disturb neighboring provinces.

literal: Men of Fen and Si came in great numbers to Hui to lodge complaints, wishing to obtain his oral judgment.
idiomatic: Men of Fen and Si came in great numbers to lodge complaints with Hui, wishing to obtain his oral judgment.

literal: He was made Governor of Qin Province; on returning to the capital, officials and people wept, clinging to his carriage, unable to stop themselves.
idiomatic: He was made governor of Qin; on returning to the capital, officials and people wept, clinging to his carriage, unable to stop themselves.

literal: Hui's carriage and horses were worn and thin—all old things from the capital; those who saw them all sighed at his integrity and frugality.
idiomatic: Hui's carriage and horses were worn and thin—all old things from the capital; onlookers sighed at his integrity and frugality.

literal: He was transferred to Director of Revenue and Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was made regular director.
idiomatic: He was transferred to director of revenue and concurrent director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was made regular director.

literal: Hui held that the law of selection aimed at obtaining the right men; limiting by years of service departed from the old body.
idiomatic: Hui held that the law of selection aimed at obtaining the right men; limiting by years of service departed from the old body.

literal: But it had been practiced long and was hard to change all at once; those equal in virtue received full years, those equal in merit advanced in virtue—men of the time called this "middling fairness."
idiomatic: But it had been practiced long and was hard to change at once; those equal in virtue received full years, those equal in merit advanced in virtue—men of the time called this middling fairness.

literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary; the rest of his offices remained as before.
idiomatic: He was made attendant-in-ordinary; the rest of his offices remained as before.

literal: Hui memorialized asking to hold only one office.
idiomatic: Hui memorialized asking to hold only one office.

literal: Scholars throughout the realm none did not sigh; all said: "Chengyang leaves selection—what may the poor still hope for!"
idiomatic: Scholars throughout the realm sighed and said, "Chengyang leaves selection—what may the poor still hope for!"

literal: The sound of complaint and lament soon reached the heights.
idiomatic: The sound of complaint and lament soon reached the heights.

literal: He was ordered back to hold Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was ordered back to hold concurrent director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At the time the Empress Dowager held sole power; court discipline was in ruins; though Hui occupied a favored post, he offered no correction.
idiomatic: At the time the Empress Dowager held sole power; court discipline was in ruins; though Hui occupied a favored post, he offered no correction.

literal: With Zheng Yan and his sort he mutually formed factions.
idiomatic: With Zheng Yan and his sort he mutually formed factions.

literal: Outwardly he seemed gentle and careful; inwardly he was full of suspicion; the smallest grudge he was sure to repay—those who understood detested him.
idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed gentle and careful; inwardly he was full of suspicion; the smallest grudge he was sure to repay—those who understood detested him.

literal: He also could not restrain his wife Lady Yu; she then had illicit relations with Prince of Guangyang Shen.
idiomatic: He also could not restrain his wife Lady Yu; she then had illicit relations with Prince of Guangyang Shen.

literal: When Shen received command of the military government, in every memorial he discussed Hui's faults; though it involved slander, much of it was also true.
idiomatic: When Shen received command of the military government, in every memorial he discussed Hui's faults; though it involved slander, much was also true.

literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, Hui was made Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, Hui was made governor of Si.

literal: Presently he was made Duke of the Secretariat, still holding the governorship.
idiomatic: Presently he was made duke of the Secretariat, still holding the governorship.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hui followed Emperor Zhuangdi on the northern tour.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hui followed Emperor Zhuangdi on the northern tour.

literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, for merit in the plot he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Marshal, and Grand Duke of the Secretariat, with plumed canopy and war drums, and his fief increased to twenty thousand households in all.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, for merit in the plot he was made attendant-in-ordinary, grand marshal, and grand duke of the Secretariat, with plumed canopy and war drums, fief increased to twenty thousand households in all.

literal: Hui memorialized declining office and enfeoffment; he did so repeatedly.
idiomatic: Hui memorialized declining office and enfeoffment repeatedly.

literal: Hui was personally favored by Emperor Zhuangdi; inwardly he feared Erzhu Rong and the others; therefore he had this declination.
idiomatic: Hui was personally favored by Emperor Zhuangdi; inwardly he feared Erzhu Rong and the others; therefore he declined.

literal: Emperor Zhuangdi understood his meaning; he permitted him to decline the enfeoffment but did not permit him to decline office.
idiomatic: The emperor understood his meaning; he permitted decline of enfeoffment but not of office.

literal: Hui's later wife was the emperor's maternal uncle's daughter.
idiomatic: Hui's later wife was the emperor's maternal uncle's daughter.

literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yu was the emperor's elder sister's husband.
idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yu was the emperor's elder sister's husband.

literal: Hui by nature was fawning and ingratiating, skilled at winning favor for himself; he relied on inside and outside connections—among the imperial clan none was more favored.
idiomatic: Hui by nature was fawning and ingratiating, skilled at winning favor; he relied on inside and outside connections—among the imperial clan none was more favored.

literal: Thereupon with Yu and the others he urged the emperor to plot against Rong.
idiomatic: Thereupon with Yu and the others he urged the emperor to plot against Rong.

literal: Emperor Zhuangdi too had long had the intention.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangdi too had long had the intention.

literal: When Rong died, Shilong and the others held their troops and would not disband.
idiomatic: When Rong died, Shilong and the others held their troops and would not disband.

literal: Hui was made Grand Guardian, still Grand Marshal, Grand Preceptor, and Recording Director, presiding over inside and outside affairs.
idiomatic: Hui was made grand guardian, still grand marshal, grand preceptor, and recording director, presiding over inside and outside affairs.

literal: Hui's original expectation was that after Rong's death the branches would scatter.
idiomatic: Hui's original expectation was that after Rong's death the branches would scatter.

literal: When the Erzhu clan gathered and plotted trouble, Hui's stratagems had no outcome; he was only fearful.
idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan gathered and plotted trouble, Hui's stratagems had no outcome; he was only fearful.

literal: By nature he was very jealous and did not wish others to stand before him.
idiomatic: By nature he was very jealous and did not wish others to stand before him.

literal: Whenever he entered to discuss strategy he alone decided with the emperor.
idiomatic: Whenever he entered to discuss strategy he alone decided with the emperor.

literal: If court officials memorialized military and state plans, he all urged the emperor not to accept.
idiomatic: If court officials memorialized military and state plans, he urged the emperor not to accept.

literal: He would say: "What worry is there that small bandits cannot be eliminated?"
idiomatic: He would say, "What worry is there that small bandits cannot be eliminated?"

literal: He also was stingy with wealth; at the time whenever there were rewards and gifts they were all thin and few, or if many they were cut down midway, given and then pursued for return.
idiomatic: He was also stingy with wealth; whenever there were rewards they were thin and few, or if many they were cut down midway, given and then pursued for return.

literal: Emperor Zhuangdi by nature was himself narrow and sparing; Hui especially approved and shaped this.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangdi by nature was narrow and sparing; Hui especially approved and shaped this.

literal: Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury Li Miao, when Hui was Duke of the Secretariat had been his marshal; Hui treated him quite generously.
idiomatic: Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury Li Miao, when Hui was duke of the Secretariat, had been his marshal; Hui treated him generously.

literal: Miao often offered loyal words; Hui mostly did not adopt them.
idiomatic: Miao often offered loyal words; Hui mostly did not adopt them.

literal: Miao told others: "Chengyang by nature has the eyes of a wasp, and now the voice of a jackal will also show."
idiomatic: Miao told others, "Chengyang by nature has the eyes of a wasp, and now the voice of a jackal will also show."

literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered, the palace guards scattered in flight; Emperor Zhuangdi walked out the Cloud Dragon Gate; Hui mounted his horse and fled across; the emperor repeatedly called him; Hui did not look back and left.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered, palace guards scattered; Emperor Zhuangdi walked out the Cloud Dragon Gate; Hui mounted and fled across; the emperor repeatedly called; Hui did not look back.

literal: He then fled to the south of the mountains, to the house of his former subordinate Kou Mi.
idiomatic: He fled to the south of the mountains, to the house of his former subordinate Kou Mi.

literal: Mi outwardly received him but inwardly was not at ease; he then frightened Hui, saying: "Official arrest is about to arrive."
idiomatic: Mi outwardly received him but inwardly was uneasy; he frightened Hui, saying, "Official arrest is about to arrive."

literal: He ordered him to avoid another place; he had men lie in wait on the road and kill him, then sent the corpse to Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: He ordered him to another place; he had men lie in wait on the road and kill him, then sent the corpse to Erzhu Zhao.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, Recording Director, and Governor of Si Province; his posthumous title was Wenxian.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made bearer of the staff, attendant-in-ordinary, grand preceptor, recording director, and governor of Si, posthumous title Wenxian.

literal: His son Yan inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Yan inherited the title.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent the rank was reduced.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent the rank was reduced.

literal: Prince of Zhangwu Tailuo died in the second year of Huangxing; posthumously made Northern Campaign Grand General and Prince of Zhangwu Commandery; his posthumous title was Jing.
idiomatic: Prince of Zhangwu Tailuo died in the second year of Huangxing; posthumously made northern campaign grand general and Prince of Zhangwu, posthumous title Jing.

literal: He had no son.
idiomatic: He had no son.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen, the second son of Prince of Nan'an Hui, Bin, was made his heir.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen, the second son of Prince of Nan'an Hui, Bin, was made his heir.

literal: Bin, courtesy name Bao'er, was brave and strong and had the talent of a general.
idiomatic: Bin, courtesy name Bao'er, was brave and strong and had the talent of a general.

literal: He was Governor of Xia Province; for greed his enfeoffment was stripped.
idiomatic: He was governor of Xia; for greed his enfeoffment was stripped.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Fen Province.
idiomatic: He was later made governor of Fen.

literal: More than six hundred Hu held difficult terrain and plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: More than six hundred Hu held difficult terrain and plotted rebellion.

literal: Bin asked for twenty thousand troops; the emperor was greatly angered and said: "If a great host is truly needed, first behead the governor, then raise the army!"
idiomatic: Bin asked for twenty thousand troops; the emperor was greatly angered and said, "If a great host is truly needed, first behead the governor, then raise the army!"

literal: Bin received the edict in great fear; he himself led the soldiers first and pacified the Hu.
idiomatic: Bin received the edict in great fear; he himself led the soldiers first and pacified the Hu.

literal: He died; posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

literal: His son Rong, courtesy name Yongxing, had a magnificent appearance and by nature was open and direct with heroic spirit.
idiomatic: His son Rong, courtesy name Yongxing, had a magnificent appearance and by nature was open and direct with heroic spirit.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu his former title was restored; he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Henan.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu his former title was restored; he rose to governor of Henan.

literal: Rong was especially greedy; he indulged in gathering wealth and was impeached by the chief commandant; his office and rank were stripped.
idiomatic: Rong was especially greedy; he indulged in gathering wealth and was impeached by the chief commandant; office and rank were stripped.

literal: The mountain Hu of Fen and Xia rebelled, linking Zhengping and Pingyang.
idiomatic: The mountain Hu of Fen and Xia rebelled, linking Zhengping and Pingyang.

literal: An edict restored Rong's former enfeoffment; he was made Eastern Campaign General, Bearer of the Staff, and Commander-in-Chief to attack them.
idiomatic: An edict restored Rong's former enfeoffment; he was made eastern campaign general, bearer of the staff, and commander-in-chief to attack them.

literal: Rong was weak in strategy and was defeated by the Hu.
idiomatic: Rong was weak in strategy and was defeated by the Hu.

literal: Later the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli raided Ying and Ding provinces; Zhangsun Chengye and others campaigned against him and failed.
idiomatic: Later the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli raided Ying and Ding; Zhangsun Chengye and others campaigned against him and failed.

literal: Rong was made General of the Imperial Chariots and vanguard left-army commander-in-chief; with Prince of Guangyang Shen and others he jointly attacked Xiuli.
idiomatic: Rong was made general of the imperial chariots and vanguard left-army commander-in-chief; with Prince of Guangyang Shen and others he jointly attacked Xiuli.

literal: The army crossed the Jiao Ford; Ge Rong killed Xiuli and set himself up; he shifted camp to Bainiu Ford; light cavalry struck Rong and killed him in the formation.
idiomatic: The army crossed the Jiao Ford; Ge Rong killed Xiuli and set himself up; he shifted camp to Bainiu Ford; light cavalry struck Rong and killed him in the formation.

literal: Posthumously made Duke of Works.
idiomatic: Posthumously made duke of works.

literal: Presently because Rong died in the prince's service, he was advanced posthumously to Duke of the Secretariat, with front and rear war drums added; his posthumous title was Zhuangwu.
idiomatic: Presently because Rong died in the prince's service, he was advanced posthumously to duke of the Secretariat with front and rear war drums added, posthumous title Zhuangwu.

literal: His son Jingzhe inherited.
idiomatic: His son Jingzhe inherited.

literal: Jingzhe's younger brother Lang was the deposed emperor.
idiomatic: Jingzhe's younger brother Lang was the deposed emperor.

literal: Prince of Leling Hu'er died in the fourth year of Heping; posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Leling; his posthumous title was Kang.
idiomatic: Prince of Leling Hu'er died in the fourth year of Heping; posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Leling, posthumous title Kang.

literal: He had no son.
idiomatic: He had no son.

literal: Emperor Xianwen ordered the second son of Hu'er's elder brother Prince of Ruyin Tiansi, Yongquan, to succeed him.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen ordered the second son of Hu'er's elder brother Prince of Ruyin Tiansi, Yongquan, to succeed him.

literal: After inheriting the enfeoffment he changed his name to Siyu.
idiomatic: After inheriting the enfeoffment he changed his name to Siyu.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Grand General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Grand General Who Pacifies the North.

literal: Mu Tai secretly plotted disloyalty; Siyu knew and did not report it; his enfeoffment was stripped and he was made a commoner.
idiomatic: Mu Tai secretly plotted disloyalty; Siyu knew and did not report it; his enfeoffment was stripped and he was made a commoner.

literal: At the end of Taihe his princely enfeoffment was restored.
idiomatic: At the end of Taihe his princely enfeoffment was restored.
